Rhea — thanks for the clear asks. Quick summary up front: yes, Redwood supports tenant-scoped accounts with a single IdP; SCIM mappings can carry a tenant_id attribute and SAML assertions can be scoped via RelayState or audience restriction. Attachment: redwood_sig_answers_v1.xlsx (answers) and scim_sample_mapping.csv (example).

Details:
- SCIM provisioning: Our SCIM endpoint accepts a custom extension attribute (urn:redwood:tenant) that we use to place a user into a particular tenant namespace on provision. If a customer configures one IdP entry but wants multiple tenant objects, they need to pass distinct tenant values for each group or user mapping. Example mapping in attached CSV.

- SAML scoping: We honor the SAML Assertion's Audience and RelayState. When RelayState is present we use it as the first-class tenant selector; absent RelayState, the Assertion's audience and a configured default_mapping are used. To avoid collisions we recommend setting RelayState per RP entry or using distinct audience URIs per tenant.

- Mitigations if IdP cannot provide tenant claim:
  * Use SCIM-based post-provisioning attribute (tenant tag) and enrollment rules in Redwood Console.
  * Enforce per-tenant username namespaces (e.g., username@tenant.example) to reduce uniqueness collisions.
  * Enable RBAC policies that are tenant-scoped — users exist globally but have no permissions until assigned to tenant-scoped roles.

I'll leave Marissa and Karthik on cc to add operational notes and the MFA scope matrix.

Regards,

Hi Rhea — adding a few operational clarifications so your auditors get the right artifact.

1) SCIM sample mapping (attached) shows the required attributes we use to decide tenant assignment: id, userName, urn:redwood:tenant (string), and groups. Minimal provisioning requires urn:redwood:tenant OR group-based mapping to an existing tenant ID. If neither is present, the user is provisioned into a quarantine namespace and flagged for admin review.

2) RBAC/least-privilege: Roles are defined per-tenant. We don't grant platform-level admin rights by default. Default role assignments on first-provision are "read-only" until an admin assigns a role. You can see the example role matrix in the SIG spreadsheet (redwood_sig_answers_v1.xlsx).

3) MFA scope: We support both IdP-enforced MFA and our own per-tenant enforcement. If a customer wants MFA for a subset of tenants, they can set tenant-level policy in Console or rely on the IdP assertion that includes the authnContext. See attached mfa_scope_matrix.pdf for how that maps to controls in the SIG.

Action items I propose:
- Alex: confirm the RelayState example we provided is acceptable to your SAML team (I've pasted a short example below).
- Rhea: if Aurora can provide one sample SAML Response with RelayState or tenant assertion, we can run a dry-provision in our staging tenant and share logs.

Example RelayState usage: POST /sso/acs?relay_state=tenant-aurora-prod — Redwood will treat that string as the tenant slug when present.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if helpful.
